errorCodes.meaning: `recordId` names no notification the community holds — never held, or discarded after it lapsed.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.
GroupId.title: GroupId

Kind.description: What the thing is. Either a registered kind — one lowerCamelCase name in the VTI specification's notification kind registry (Appendix G), such as `election` — or an unregistered kind, written `<reverse-DNS domain>:<name>` under a domain its definer controls, such as `org.example:meetingInvite`. A recipient that does not recognise a kind holds, lists and discards it and does nothing else with it (VTI-NTF-012).
Kind.title: Kind

Notification.description: The members of one notification, as notifications/notify carries them and as a recipient's agent records them. The originator is the `issuer` of the notifications/notify document and the addressee its `recipient`; neither is repeated here, because the originator's proof covers both.

audience.description: The DID whose holders or members the thing concerns — for an election under a credential roll, the DID the roll names (`roll.memberOf`); otherwise the community's own. It says whom the thing is for, not that the recipient is one of them: a recipient may be the audience itself, or a party the audience relayed the notification to.

relayable.description: Whether the addressee may relay this notification to the parties it stands for (notifications/relay). The originator states it explicitly; an addressee MUST NOT relay a notification whose `relayable` is false, or whose kind may not be relayed (VTI-NTF-041).

revision.description: The revision of this notification. A recipient replaces the record it holds with a higher revision and leaves it unchanged for an equal or lower one (VTI-NTF-022). The first revision is 1.

validFrom.description: When the thing can first be acted on — for an election, when voting opens. Absent: it can be acted on now.

validUntil.description: When the thing can no longer be acted on, and the notification lapses — for an election, when voting closes. A recipient discards a notification received after it (VTI-NTF-032). Absent: the kind's definition says when it lapses.

Notification.title: Notification

NotificationId.description: The originator's identifier for one notification, unique among the notifications that originator issues and the same in every document that carries it — retries, re-issued documents and relayed copies alike. It is the notification's idempotency key (VTI-NTF-021). Compared for equality only. An originator SHOULD make it unguessable and SHOULD NOT make it descriptive: it travels as far as the notification does.
NotificationId.title: NotificationId

ReceivedNotification.description: One notification the community holds, as an administrator with `vtc.notifications.read` sees it. `originator`, `deliveredBy` and every entry of `relayedBy` were verified by the community when it accepted the notification (VTI-NTF-042); an administrator that does not take the community's word for them reads the document with vtc/notifications/show and verifies it.

mayRelay.description: Whether the community may relay the revision held now: its `relayable` is true, its kind may be relayed, the received chain carries at most three relays so that the community's own makes at most four (VTI-NTF-041), and it is neither withdrawn nor past its `validUntil`.

notification.description: The notification's members at the revision held.

originator.description: The issuer of the notifications/notify document: who said the thing exists.

receivedAt.description: When the community accepted the revision held.

relayDecisions.description: The relay decisions made for this notification, oldest first. Empty while none has been. Every later revision, a withdrawal included, is relayed to every party an earlier one was, without a new decision (VTI-NTF-044).

relayDisclosure.description: What a relay of the notification discloses about the community, as the kind's definition states it (VTI-NTF-046) — for the kind `election`, that the community is a member of the community holding the election. Present exactly when the kind's definition says a relay discloses something; the administrator deciding a relay is shown it, and acknowledges it in vtc/notifications/relay.

relayedBy.description: The relayers the held revision passed through before it reached the community, in the order they relayed it; the last delivered it here, and is the party the acceptance policy counted (VTI-NTF-031). Empty for a notification the originator sent the community directly.

ReceivedNotification.title: ReceivedNotification

RecipientScope.description: Which of the community's members a relay decision reaches: `allMembers` — every active member; `group` — the active members of one community group; `role` — the active members holding one community role.
RecipientScope.title: RecipientScope

Recipients.description: The members a relay decision reaches, resolved by the community from its own records when the decision is made (VTI-NTF-072). `groupId` is present exactly when `scope` is `group`, and `role` exactly when `scope` is `role`. Whatever the scope, the community never relays to itself, to the notification's originator, or to any relayer the received chain names (VTI-NTF-047), and relays to each party at most once per revision.

groupId.description: The community group whose active members the relay reaches.

role.description: The community role whose active holders the relay reaches, in the wire form the community's member records use — for example `moderator`, or `custom:editor`.

Recipients.title: Recipients

RecordId.description: The community's own identifier for one received notification, stable across the revisions that replace it. Opaque and compared for equality only; unguessable, because a read by a caller without the capability is refused and an enumerable identifier would turn the refusal into an oracle.
RecordId.title: RecordId

RelayDecision.description: One administrator's decision to relay a received notification, as the community records it (VTI-NTF-073). It records the selection and how many parties it added, never who they are: the record of whom the community relayed to exists only to relay later revisions to them (VTI-NTF-044).

recipientCount.description: How many parties this decision added to those the notification is relayed to. Parties an earlier decision already reached are not counted again.

RelayDecision.title: RelayDecision

document.description: The document that delivered the revision held, kept whole and exactly as received — proof included: the notifications/notify/0.1 document, or the outermost notifications/relay/0.1 document. An opaque object, so that every member its issuer signed survives unchanged for the administrator to verify. It is also what a relay carries in `forwarded`.

Status.description: Whether the thing is still open to the audience: `available`, or `withdrawn` — cancelled by its holder, or no longer open to the audience — in which case the recipient keeps the record only to show that it was withdrawn (VTI-NTF-024).
Status.title: Status

Subject.description: Where the thing is and how to open it. Only these three members: what the thing contains is shown by its holder, to a reader it admits, when the thing is opened with `openWith`.

heldBy.description: The DID of the party holding the thing — for an election, the community. The party a recipient sends `openWith` to.

id.description: The thing's identifier at `heldBy`, in the form the `openWith` task takes it — for an election, its `electionId`.

openWith.description: The Type URI of the Trust Task by which a recipient opens the thing at `heldBy` — for an election, `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/elections/show/0.6`. A recipient opens it only at its principal's choice (VTI-NTF-053), and only by a version of that task it and `heldBy` both serve.

Subject.title: Subject

schema.description: An administrator with `vtc.notifications.read` reads one notification the community holds as its addressee, with the document that delivered it exactly as received — the notifications/notify document, or the notifications/relay document carrying it — so the administrator can verify the originator's proof and every relay before deciding a relay (VTI-NTF-070). A read changes nothing, and sends nothing to anyone. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.
schema.title: VTC Notifications — Show — payload
